mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE has been above 4.0% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based contraction in consumer demand, which triggers a sell-off in equities as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS for two consecutive months fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases (i.e., Rank IC < 0.03 or negative returns occur in less than 45% of such cases).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS rising above 3.0% for three consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 days as higher borrowing costs dampen corporate investment and consumer spending.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS has been above 3.0% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past three months indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO has increased for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 5.0% year-over-year, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change exceeds 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and employment (PAYEMS) indicate a labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in UNRATE and PAYEMS for two consecutive months fails to predict negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (i.e., Rank IC < 0.03 or negative returns occur in less than 45% of such cases).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100 for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days as manufacturing slowdowns signal weakening economic activity and reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO has been below 100 for two consecutive months.
